description: Cross-references three distinct 'dominant partition' notions across the codebase: (1) Path A u-pole hook λ_⋆(Z, N) = (Z+2N+1, 1^{2Z+N-1}); (2) PR #639 operator-valued Φ_q failure-dominant (per per-partition-k-lambda-rule.md); (3) SDP shadow-price argmax (per probe-sdp-active-set-dominant-partition).  Tests the hypothesis: PR #639 dominant = lump_column(Path-A hook), i.e., the operator-binding partition is a structural function of the Markov-trace pole-maximizer hook.

verdict.interpretation: The Path A hook λ_⋆(Z,N) is the u-pole maximizer of tr_M — a property of the Markov trace's leading singularity at q → 0.  Empirically the lump_column(hook) operation reproduces PR #639's operator-Φ_q failure-dominant partition at T and ³He but NOT D, suggesting the relationship is structural for A = 3 atoms (n = 9 strands) but fails for the A = 2 deuteron.  The SDP shadow-price argmax is a separate optimisation (LP duality on the operator-selection problem) and does not in general match either.
